summary: This tutorial introduces Mozilla Thunderbird, a simple email client available on various operating systems. It covers downloading and launching Thunderbird, configuring new email accounts, reading and writing emails, and sending messages. Thunderbird supports multiple email accounts and categorizes messages by date, sender, priority, or custom labels. The tutorial demonstrates setting up Thunderbird on Ubuntu Linux 12.04. To install Thunderbird, users can use the Ubuntu Software Center or download it from the Mozilla website. For Windows users, Thunderbird is compatible with MS Windows XP, 7, and newer versions. Users need at least two valid email accounts to use Thunderbird and ensure their email accounts support POP3 options. Launching Thunderbird involves clicking the Thunderbird icon on the dash home button. Configuring email accounts requires logging into each account, enabling POP3, and configuring settings for message downloading. The interface includes a main menu with options and shortcuts, and the application is divided into two panels showing folders and advanced features.
